newsitem.title: UK: UK's PIA steps up drive against pension misselling.
newsitem.headline: UK's PIA steps up drive against pension misselling.

text.p: Britain's Personal Investment Authority (PIA) is stepping up pressure on insurance companies to resolve outstanding cases of pension mis-selling in a series of meetings with the worst offenders.
Industry sources said the PIA was holding a series of meetings with firms with a large number of cases yet to be settled to get them to outline their plans to clear up the backlog.
The PIA, which regulates the sale of investment products to the public, declined to comment.
Pension mis-selling has affected several hundred thousand people who may have been wrongly advised to take out personal pensions by financial companies during the late 1980s and early 1990s.
The review into the mis-selling was launched by the top financial regulator the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) in 1994 but progress has been slow.

On Tuesday Britain's largest insurer, Prudential Corp, said it had reached agreement with Britain's GMB general union to compensate some victims of personal pensions mis-selling and bring an end to litigation in the courts.
